reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-07). 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) were built from accepted ACTUAL reads, not estimates (E-04), and neither a tariff change (E-03) nor degraded response times (E-02) occurred, indicating the billing import/validation step itself began producing systematic bill errors around August regardless of read source. In parallel, manual meter-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts (E-01), driving estimate-substitution errors for the remaining ~41% of disputed bills.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-07). Of the 1240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (out of 3025 total, E-04), 1184 are AMI reads that arrived on time and were exported to billing but were rejected at import with billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, not missed field routes or AMI non-arrival (only 56 were true non-arrivals) (E-11). This coincides with billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, which compares raw meter register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-12), while AMI firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) reports registers in units of 0.1 m3 rather than m3 (E-13) - so genuine, on-time reads from v4.2 meters are misread as abnormal high consumption, rejected, and billed as estimates, driving the estimate-substitution bucket of the dispute surge.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
